details.description:

a line extending from 12 miles north of Ticaboo to 11 miles southwest
of Halls Crossing to near Rainbow Bridge South Trailhead. Movement
was west at 30 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts of 50 to 55 mph.

details.instruction:

the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose

should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

title: Flood Watch
location: SW Kenai Peninsula; NW Kenai Peninsula

details.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...The following areas, Western Kenai Peninsula.  This
includes the cities of Homer, Anchor Point, Ninilchik, Clam Gulch,
Kenai, Soldotna, Sterling, And Nikiski.

* WHEN...From Tuesday morning through Wednesday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas. Water levels for the Kenai and
Anchor Rivers remain elevated from the previous rain event and
will likely rise again during this next rain event.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rain is expected to develop south to north across the western
Kenai Peninsula by late Tuesday morning and continue through
early Wednesday morning before tapering off. 0.75" to 1.25"
of rain is likely (70-80%) with this system with a low chance
(20%) for amounts greater than 1.25" around Anchor Point and
the Homer Bluffs. The highest rainfall amounts are expected
from Ninilchik south to Homer. For the Kenai area, rainfall
amounts around 0.4" to 0.7" are likely (70-80%).

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
details.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

title: Flood Watch
location: Hatcher Pass; Western Susitna Valley; Southern Susitna Valley; Central Susitna Valley; Northern Susitna Valley

details.description:

* WHERE...The following areas, Susitna Valley and Hatcher Pass. This
includes the cities of Skwentna, Willow, Talkeetna, Trapper Creek,
Petersville, and Chulitna.

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Low-water
crossings may be flooded. Area rivers, creeks, and streams are
elevated from the previous rain event and will likely rise again
during these next rain events.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Two additional storm systems will bring rain to the Susitna
Valley, the first Tuesday afternoon through Wednesday morning
and the second Wednesday evening through Thursday afternoon.
0.50" to 1" of rain is likely (70-80%) with the first event
with an additional 1.0" to 2.5" of rain likely (70-80%) with
the second event. The track of both systems will favor the
highest rainfall totals over the northern and eastern
Susitna, along the Talkeetna Mountains. As a result, fast
responding rivers and streams along and east of the Parks
Highway may be more susceptible to flooding with this event.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar.

drainage and low-lying areas.

details.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

dangers of flooding.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where

title: Rip Current Statement
location: Escambia Coastal; Santa Rosa Coastal; Okaloosa Coastal

details.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 8
to 11 feet expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Escambia Coastal, Santa Rosa Coastal and Okaloosa
Coastal Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Thursday
night. For the High Surf Warning, from 1 PM this afternoon to
6 AM CDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Breaking waves can sweep people off jetties and
docks, and into dangerous seas. Life-threatening swimming
conditions and significant beach erosion can be expected. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.
details.instruction:
Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

title: Heat Advisory
location: Montague; Jack; Wise; Palo Pinto; Parker; Hood; Somervell; Johnson; Ellis; Henderson; Bosque; Hill; Navarro; Freestone; Anderson; Bell; McLennan; Falls; Limestone; Leon; Milam; Robertson

details.description:
* WHAT...Heat index values up to 108 and temperatures up to 103.

* WHERE...Portions of north central, northeast, and south central
Texas.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM CDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures and high humidity will increase the risk
for heat-related illnesses to occur, particularly for those working
or participating in outdoor activities.
details.instruction:
Take extra precautions when outside by staying hydrated, wearing
lightweight and loose fitting clothing, and limiting strenuous
activities to the early morning or evening. Check up on relatives and
neighbors. Never leave young children or pets in an enclosed vehicle,
even for a short time, as temperatures can quickly rise to
life-threatening levels.

Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat stroke. To
reduce risk when outdoors, the occupational safety and health
administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in shaded
or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat should be
moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an emergency!
Call 911 ASAP if you or someone you know is exhibiting signs of heat
stroke.

resources or dial 2-1-1 in Texas.

title: Flash Flood Warning
location: Santa Cruz, AZ

details.description:
FFWTWC

The National Weather Service in Tucson has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
South Central Santa Cruz County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until 115 AM MST.

* At 1012 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 0.5 and 1.5 inches of
rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Nogales, Rio Rico, Nogales International Airport and Kino Springs.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 19 between mile markers 1 and 13. Route 82 between mile
markers 1 and 10.

This includes the following Flash Flood Prone Locations...
Nogales Wash at Doe St Bridge and Pendleton Dr at Sonoita Creek.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Sonoita Creek, Potrero Creek and Santa Cruz River.
details.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

title: Heat Advisory
location: Fisher; Haskell; Throckmorton; Jones; Shackelford; Taylor; Callahan

details.description:
* WHAT...Heat index values will approach 105.

* WHERE...Callahan, Fisher, Haskell, Jones, Shackelford, Taylor, and
Throckmorton Counties.

* WHEN...From 1 PM to 8 PM CDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures and high humidity may cause heat
illnesses.
details.instruction:
A Heat Advisory means that hot weather conditions are occurring or
expected. This will create a situation in which heat illnesses are
possible.

Never, ever, leave children or pets alone in enclosed vehicles, not
even for a few minutes. Car interiors can reach lethal temperatures
in a matter of minutes.

Stay indoors and seek air-conditioned buildings. Drink water more
than usual, and avoid dehydrating alcoholic, sugary, or caffeinated
drinks. Dress for the heat by wearing lightweight and light colored
clothing. Eat small meals and eat more often. Monitor those with a
higher vulnerability to heat, including small children. Check in on
family, friends, and neighbors, especially the elderly. If engaging
in outdoor activity, take longer and more frequent breaks and avoid
the hottest parts of the day.

title: Heat Advisory
location: Beaver; Ochiltree

details.description:
* WHAT...Heat index values up to 105 expected with some know hotter
locations experience actual temperatures above 105.

* WHERE...In Oklahoma, Beaver County. In Texas, Ochiltree County.

* WHEN...From 1 PM to 9 PM CDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures and high humidity may cause heat
illnesses.
details.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

title: Flood Advisory
location: Pima, AZ

details.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northeastern Pima County in southeastern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1145 PM MST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Overflowing poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 939 PM MST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain due to thunderstorms. This  will cause urban and small
stream flooding. Between 0.5 and 1.2 inches of rain have fallen.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Robles Wash, Los, Oro, Caada del, Big Wash, Indian Well Wash,
Santa Cruz River, Chalk Creek, Rillito River and Guild Wash.
Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.8 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Oro Valley, Marana, Casas Adobes, Tortolita and Dove Mountain.
- This includes the following highways...
Route 77 between mile markers 75 and 79. Interstate 10 between
mile markers 233 and 248.

This includes the following Flash Flood Prone Locations...
Overton Rd at Canada del Oro.
